text:
sam: hey team, first day — trying to get into the edge-research namespace but I keep getting Forbidden when listing pods.
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "sam" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "edge-research". Any quick fixes?

maya: welcome! :wave: first step, can you confirm your context: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config view --minify`?

sam: current-context is `redwood-dev` and kubeconfig came from the onboarding portal. output of `kubectl config view --minify` looks normal. still forbidden.

dev-infra: @sam can you run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n edge-research --as=system:serviceaccount:edge-research:onboard-sa` and paste the output here? that tells us if the serviceaccount has perms.

sam: ran that, it returns: 

"no"

so seems like SA also doesn't have list perms?

priya: we typically lock those namespaces down. to debug whether it's your user vs namespace RBAC, try impersonation:

`kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:edge-research:onboard-sa auth can-i list pods -n edge-research`

if that returns `yes`, your user is blocked; if `no`, the rolebinding for onboard-sa is missing.

olivia: if you want temp access while we audit, we can create a RoleBinding for your user scoped to view. example we would run: 

`kubectl create rolebinding onboarding-sam-view --clusterrole=view --user=sam -n edge-research`

but please file an infra ticket so we can track it and auto-revoke. @dev-infra can approve the change.

dev-infra: i'll do a short-lived grant but prefer doing the service-account token flow for troubleshooting first. sam, try this flow:

```bash
# (1) try to create a token for onboard-sa if cluster supports it
kubectl -n edge-research create token onboard-sa
# (2) copy the token and make a temp kubeconfig user
kubectl config set-credentials sam-onboard --token=<PASTE_TOKEN>
kubectl config set-context temp-onboard --cluster=redwood-dev --namespace=edge-research --user=sam-onboard
kubectl config use-context temp-onboard
kubectl get pods -n edge-research
```

If `create token` errors (older k8s), fallback to pulling the secret token.

sam: tried the token command, got `error: unable to create token: serviceaccount "onboard-sa" not found` — maybe there isn't an onboard-sa in that ns. i can paste full error if helpful.

priya: ok, if there is no onboard-sa created, we can either create one or just bind your user. alternative secret-based token (ugh) would be: 

`kubectl -n edge-research get sa onboard-sa -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}'`
`kubectl -n edge-research get secret <SECRET_NAME> -o go-template='{{.data.token}}' | base64 -d`

but i agree that's messy. i'll coordinate with @dev-infra to do a temporary rolebinding and then create an audited onboarding SA for future hires.

devex-bot: Incident-note: Temporary rolebinding `onboarding-sam-view` created by dev-infra for 2h. Audit ticket: INF-5423.

sam: can see pods now, thanks! :tada: quick follow-up — what's the canonical process to request longer-term access for a team member? is there a template?

maya: open an infra access request (Zendesk) and use the "k8s namespace access" template. include: namespace name, justification, duration, owner, and whether CI needs write permissions. link: https://intra.redwood.com/infra-access-requests

priya: also ping #eng-oncall and #devex when you submit so we can triage faster. we'll add this flow to the new-hire checklist and create a short doc with the token vs rolebinding options.

dev-infra: :thumbsup: closing the loop here — welcome to Redwood, @sam! we'll follow up in the ticket with the audit entries and a permanent onboarding SA for edge-research.
